about.title: About us
about.lead: Codo Hub is a platform for Kazakh-speaking developers: write code, share projects and learn together in one place.

sections.title: What is Codo Hub?
sections.text: Codo Hub is a developer workspace that runs in the browser. Write your project, run it and share it with others — no extra software to install.

sections.title: Our mission
sections.text: Make programming accessible in Kazakh: the interface, the assistant and the community all speak our language. We build a place where beginners and experienced developers learn from each other.

sections.title: What you can do
items: Vibecoding IDE — in-browser editor, files and live preview
Terminal — a shell in the project folder: tabs, split, run menu
Burkit AI — an assistant that writes code, shows diffs and explains errors
Notes — notes with links, a graph and a canvas
Chat and groups — talk and share project cards
Codes — publish, browse and share projects

sections.title: Our values
items: Native language — the interface and assistant speak Kazakh (Russian and English too)
Openness — we encourage sharing knowledge and code
Security — passwords are hashed, API keys are stored encrypted
Community — every project can inspire someone

sections.title: Get in touch
sections.text: Have an idea, a question or found a bug? Write to us on the Contact page. We read every message.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: By using Codo Hub you agree to the terms below. We tried to keep them short and clear.

sections.title: Acceptance
sections.text: Signing up or using the site means you accept these terms and the Privacy policy. If you have questions or suggestions about the terms, write to us on the Contact page.

sections.title: Your account
sections.text: You are responsible for keeping your account secure.
items: Use a real email address
Never share your password; turn on two-factor authentication if you can
Do not impersonate anyone
You can delete your account at any time in Settings

sections.title: Acceptable use
sections.text: Use the service to learn, build and share.
items: Publish code you own or are allowed to distribute
Respect other users

sections.title: Other people’s code
sections.text: You can use another user’s code only to improve (edit) it.
items: Your edited version is saved only for you — you cannot upload or publish it under your name
You can send your changes to the code owner — the owner decides whether to accept them
To use the code in your own project, ask the owner for authorship rights (permission)

sections.title: Prohibited
items: Spreading malware, viruses, phishing or scams
Uploading or publishing someone else’s code under your name
Using the terminal or servers for attacks, mining or bypassing limits
Spam, insults, harassment and illegal content
Trying to access other people’s accounts or data without permission

sections.title: Terminal and Burkit AI
sections.text: The terminal runs in your private workspace with resource limits. Burkit’s answers are AI-generated and may be wrong — review code before using it. If you add your own API key, its costs and terms are between you and the key provider.

sections.title: Intellectual property
sections.text: Code and notes you publish remain yours; by publishing you allow us to display them on the site. The Codo Hub name, logo and interface belong to the platform.

sections.title: Limitation of liability
sections.text: The service is provided “as is”. We aim for reliable operation but cannot guarantee uptime or that data is never lost — keep backups of important projects.

sections.title: Suspension
sections.text: If the terms are violated, we may remove content or suspend the account temporarily or permanently.

sections.title: Changes
sections.text: These terms may be updated. We will announce important changes on the site; continuing to use the service after an update means you accept the new version.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: We collect only the data the service needs to work, and we never sell it.

sections.title: What we collect
items: Account: username, email and a password hash (the password itself is never stored)
Content: codes, Vibecoding projects, Notes, chat messages
Burkit: chat history and, if you add one, your API key (encrypted)
Technical: sign-in times, IP address and error logs — for security

sections.title: How we use it
items: Signing you in and protecting your account
Storing your projects and syncing them across devices
Sending emails: password reset and important notices
Improving the service and preventing abuse

sections.title: Third-party services
sections.text: Some features rely on external services:
items: Google Gemini — your Burkit prompts and attached code are sent to get an answer
Google Firebase — data storage and sync
Sign in with Google — only if you choose it

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
sections.text: We use a protected (HttpOnly) cookie to keep you signed in. Preferences such as language, theme and open tabs are stored in your browser’s localStorage. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.title: Security
sections.text: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, API keys are stored encrypted, and traffic goes over HTTPS. The terminal runs in each user’s private folder with limits.

sections.title: Your rights
items: View your data and edit it in your profile
Delete codes and notes at any time
Delete your account completely in Settings
Contact us with questions about your data

sections.title: Contact
sections.text: If you have privacy questions, write to us on the Contact page.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lead: Questions, ideas or bug reports — we are happy to hear them all.
contact.replyHint: We usually reply within 1–2 business days

cli.desc: Upload projects from the terminal (codo CLI)
cli.howText: codo is a tool you install once that works like Git: stage your changes, commit them, push to the site. Only Python 3.8+ is needed.
cli.note: The first push creates the project on the site; later pushes update it (only changed files are sent). Junk and caches (node_modules, __pycache__, .git, venv…) are never sent; list other files to skip in .codoignore. Handy: codo status — what changed, codo log — commits, codo uninstall — remove from this computer.
